title: What Does Airbnb Photography Cost in Austin? (2026 Rates)
description: What short-term rental photography actually costs in Austin, TX in 2026 — market rates, what moves the price, and when the cheaper option costs more.
h1: What Airbnb Photography Costs in Austin

body: Short answer: $150 to $425 for a standard Austin short-term rental, depending on bedroom count and add-ons. The spread is wide because the market has three distinct tiers that do not sell the same thing.

blocks.heading: Austin market rates, 2026
rows: 15–25 photos, phone or entry DSLR, often no perspective correction, 3–7 day turnaround
25–50 edited photos, wide-angle body, corrected verticals, 24–72 hour turnaround
50+ photos, twilight and aerial included, staging direction, 48–72 hours
blocks.note: Reference points drawn from Austin MLS listing rates ($150–325, ~$185 median) and short-term rental shoots ($100–400 standard).

blocks.heading: What actually moves the price
body: Bedroom count is the main driver, because it sets both shoot time and photo count. A studio is one room and a bathroom. A 4BR is nine or ten spaces that each need two or three usable angles.

Add-ons are the second driver. Aerial drone work runs $95 to $400 across this market, with the typical Austin add-on around $148, depending on whether the operator is Part 107 licensed and whether the property sits inside controlled airspace. A large share of Austin — anything near Bergstrom or under the Class C shelf — requires LAANC authorization, and shooters without it either skip the aerial or fly it illegally. Twilight sessions run $125 to $400, and the spread is mostly about model: a twilight add-on shot on the same trip as the day photos is far cheaper than a separate evening callout.
Travel is the third. Most Austin shooters include the urban core and charge past Lakeway, Dripping Springs or Georgetown.

blocks.heading: When cheap costs more
body: The specific failure of a sub-$150 shoot is almost never sharpness. It is two things: uncorrected perspective, where the walls bow outward from an over-wide lens and the room reads as distorted, and blown windows, where every exterior view is a white rectangle.

Both are fixable in post by someone who knows how, and neither is fixed by a better camera. If a quote is unusually low, ask to see a full set from one property rather than a portfolio of best frames — the giveaway is in the fifteenth photo, not the first.

blocks.heading: The number that actually matters
body: A shoot is a one-time cost against a recurring nightly rate. On an Austin unit at a $180 average nightly rate, a $195 shoot is covered by roughly one extra booked night. The question is not whether $195 is cheap in the abstract — it is whether the photo set books one more night per year than what you have now.

title: Austin Short-Term Rental License Rules for Your Listing
description: What Austin's short-term rental licensing rules mean for your Airbnb listing — the occupancy cap, the delisting timeline, and what to update now.
h1: Austin Short-Term Rental Licensing and Your Listing

body: We are photographers, not attorneys or license consultants. This page covers one narrow thing: what Austin's licensing shake-up changes about the listing itself — the copy, the capacity you advertise, and the photos. For the licensing process, the City of Austin is the only source that counts, and it is linked at the bottom of this page.
Everything factual below is sourced and dated. If you are reading this well after the check date, verify before acting.

blocks.heading: Where things actually stand
body: Since 1 July 2026, Airbnb, VRBO and other platforms must carry a license field on every Austin listing, must remove a listing within 10 days of a City delist request, and may not collect booking fees on an unlicensed rental.

But enforcement is phased, not instant. The City paused mass delist notices for roughly six months after its new licensing system launched in May 2026, and said it would phase them in starting with properties that generate nuisance complaints. In practice that means the window has been open through most of 2026 and is closing rather than closed.

The scale is not small. As of May 2026 the City estimated 3,000 to 4,000 Austin short-term rentals were operating without a valid license, having already identified roughly 2,785 unlicensed addresses by 1 April. Penalties run $500 per offense, per day, with each day counted separately.

blocks.heading: What the City charges
rows: 9% occupancy plus 2% venue project; platforms have collected this automatically since April 2025
blocks.note: Fees and license types (Type 1, Type 2 Residential, Type 2 Commercial, Type 3) as published by Austin Development Services. Apply online through Austin Finance Online, in person at the Permitting and Development Center, or by mail.

blocks.heading: The change most listings have not made yet
body: Austin now enforces an occupancy formula of two guests per bedroom plus two additional guests, capped at ten people per unit regardless of size.

That is the rule most likely to have quietly invalidated your listing. A 4-bedroom advertised as sleeping 12 is now advertising above the cap. A 2-bedroom listed at 8 is over. The number in your listing title, the number in your description, the guest slider, and the photos showing the bed configuration all need to agree with the formula — and for a lot of Austin listings written before the change, they do not.

This is the one place where the licensing story and a photo set genuinely meet. If the sleeping arrangement you show no longer matches the capacity you are allowed to sell, both the copy and the images are out of date.

blocks.heading: What to reconcile on your listing
blocks.intro: Working through this costs nothing and is worth doing whether or not you use us:
items: Recalculate your maximum: (2 × bedrooms) + 2, capped at 10. Compare it to the guest count your listing currently sells.
Update the guest slider, the title, and any 'sleeps N' claim in the description to match.
Check that the beds shown in your photos match the configuration you now advertise. A sofa bed you no longer count should not be the hero of a frame.
Add your license number to the platform's license field rather than waiting to be asked.
If you removed beds to come under the cap, the rooms they were in need reshooting — an empty corner where a bed used to be reads as a mistake.
Check the amenity list against what is actually in the property today. Enforcement attention tends to arrive alongside complaint attention.

blocks.heading: What a shrinking market means for the listings that stay
body: Austin's active listing count fell about 11% year over year to roughly 17,165 as of July 2026, while occupancy rose almost 9%. Fewer listings are absorbing similar demand.

For a licensed operator that is the favourable side of a bad-sounding statistic. The casual hosts most likely to exit are the ones who were never going to invest in the listing anyway, and the guests who would have booked them are still coming to Austin. Whether that demand lands on your listing or your neighbour's is decided in the search results, where the photo is the entire first impression.
If you are re-listing after sorting out a license, you are re-entering a thinner market. That is the moment the listing is worth getting right rather than restoring as it was.

blocks.heading: Where we come in, honestly
body: We shoot short-term rentals. We cannot file your license, we cannot advise you on which type you need, and we would be the wrong people to ask. What we can do is make the listing you relaunch better than the one that came down — flat rates by bedroom count, 24 to 72 hour turnaround, and full rights to the images.

If your listing already reflects the occupancy rule and the photos still represent the property accurately, you do not need us for this. Nothing on this page is a reason to book a shoot you would not otherwise book.

title: How to Prep Your Airbnb for a Photo Shoot | Austin Checklist
description: A room-by-room prep checklist for short-term rental photography. What to do the night before and the morning of so the shoot is worth what you paid for it.
h1: How to Prep Your Airbnb for Photos

body: Preparation is worth more to the final photo set than any add-on on the price list. A well-prepped $195 studio outshoots a cluttered $425 house every time. This is the list we send clients before a shoot.

blocks.heading: The night before
blocks.intro: Do these when you have time. They take longer than you think.
items: Wash and press all bed linen. Wrinkles are the single most visible flaw in a listing photo and cannot be retouched cheaply.
Replace every dead bulb, and match colour temperature across the unit — one yellow bulb in a room of white ones turns the whole frame green.
Clear all countertops completely. Kitchen and bathroom counters photograph best empty, then styled back with one or two deliberate objects.
Remove personal items, mail, chargers, remotes, bins and pet bowls from every room.
Clean the interior of all windows and mirrors. Both show every mark under a wide lens.
Cut fresh greenery or buy a single simple arrangement. One is enough for the whole unit.

blocks.heading: The morning of
items: Make every bed hotel-tight, then steam or hand-smooth the duvet one more time.
Open all blinds and curtains fully and level them to the same height.
Turn every light on, including lamps and range hoods, before we arrive.
Set the thermostat display to something neutral and hide the remote.
Park cars away from the front elevation and roll the bins out of frame.
Sweep or blow the porch, patio and pool deck.
Put toilet seats down and lids closed, and hang fresh, matching towels.

blocks.heading: The three things people forget
body: Ceiling fans. Turn them off — a spinning fan blurs into a grey disc and ruins the frame.
Cords. Route phone chargers, lamp cords and console cables behind furniture. They are invisible to you and glaring in a photo.
The shower. It gets photographed, it is usually the least-prepped surface in the unit, and hard-water spotting on Austin's water shows up clearly on glass.

blocks.heading: What you do not need to do
body: Do not buy furniture for the shoot. Do not repaint. Do not stage a fruit bowl you will remove an hour later — guests notice the gap between the photos and the reality, and that gap shows up in reviews. Shoot the property you actually rent, at its best.

title: Short-Term Rental Photography Austin | Airbnb & VRBO
description: Short-term rental photography for Austin operators — Airbnb, VRBO, Booking.com and direct-booking sites. Flat rates, 24–72 hour delivery, full commercial rights.

body: Short-term rental photography is not real estate photography with a different label. A listing photo is not selling a building, it is selling a stay — which changes what gets shot, how many frames the set needs, and what order they go in.

Real estate photography sells the floor plan: wide, empty, architectural. Short-term rental photography sells the experience: the bed you sleep in, the counter you make coffee on, the patio where the evening happens. Sets that are shot like MLS listings underperform on Airbnb, and the reason is that they answer the wrong questions.

blocks.heading: What a complete set covers
body: Every bedroom with the bed as the subject. Every bathroom including the shower interior. The kitchen wide and one detail frame. The living space from two angles. Every outdoor space. The workspace, if there is one — remote-work filtering is now a meaningful share of Austin booking traffic. Parking and entry, so arrival is not a mystery. And one hero frame that carries the whole listing.

blocks.heading: Ordered for upload
body: Airbnb weights the first five photos heavily, and most owners upload in whatever order the folder happens to sort. Sets are delivered numbered in booking order — hero, living, kitchen, primary bedroom, then the rest — so you can drag the folder in and it is already right.

blocks.heading: Rates
blocks.note: Same flat rates across Airbnb, VRBO, Booking.com and direct-booking use.

items.q: Can I use these on VRBO and my own site too?
items.a: Yes. You get full commercial rights with no per-platform licensing. Use them anywhere, including paid ads.
We shoot between guests. A turnover window right after the cleaner finishes is the ideal slot — the unit is already staged and there is nobody in it.

items.q: What about property managers with multiple units?
items.a: Portfolio rates are quoted per portfolio rather than per unit. Over three properties, get in touch and we will price the whole set.
Short-form vertical video is available and quoted with the shoot. Airbnb does not host video on listings, but it is worth having for Instagram and a direct-booking site.
